analysis.investment_thesis: Nesco is a quality asset — a near-monopoly Mumbai exhibition + IT-park business with 50%+ operating margins and historically zero debt — but at ~5.1% earnings yield (EBIT ₹438 Cr / EV ~₹8,610 Cr) it falls short of Greenblatt's 6%+ attractive threshold. The ROIC of ~21% (per ROCE) clears the 20% bar, but with only one of two Magic Formula legs firmly planted, it ranks middle-of-the-pack, not top-decile.
key_strengths: Near-monopoly exhibition venue in Mumbai with 50.9% operating margins — rare, durable asset that prints cash
Historically debt-free (D/E 0.04) with 9-year revenue CAGR of 12% and consistently positive OCF (5/5 years)
ROCE of 21% meets Magic Formula threshold; high-margin IT park segment diversifies recurring income
key_risks: Massive capex surge: CWIP exploded from ₹162 Cr (2024) to ₹761 Cr (2025), turning FCF sharply negative at -₹435 Cr — capital destruction risk until assets monetise
Earnings yield of ~5.1% is below Greenblatt's 6% floor, meaning the market is pricing in quality but leaving no margin of safety
Conglomerate structure (exhibitions + IT park + food + engineering) dilutes ROIC vs. a pure-play; the industrial/engineering segment earns far lower returns
red_flags: FY2025 FCF turned deeply negative (-₹435 Cr) due to ₹784 Cr capex — largest single-year spend in company history with return timeline uncertain
First meaningful borrowing (₹110 Cr) appeared in FY2025 after years of zero debt — signals the capex is straining the balance sheet
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula on Nesco: EBIT (operating income) FY2025 = ₹438 Cr; EV ≈ ₹8,514 Cr market cap + ₹110 Cr borrowings – ₹14 Cr cash = ~₹8,610 Cr. That yields an earnings yield of just 5.1% — below my 6% minimum and well below the 12-15% zone where I get excited. Using ROCE as a ROIC proxy (the data doesn't break out net working capital cleanly), the company clears 21% — barely above my 20% threshold. So one leg of the formula works; the other doesn't. At EV/EBITDA of 15x and P/E of 20.8x, the market is already paying a fair-to-full price for Nesco's quality, leaving little room for the kind of "aha, the market is wrong" opportunity the Magic Formula is designed to exploit.

The business itself is genuinely good: a hard-to-replicate convention centre in one of India's most land-constrained cities, 85%+ gross margins, near-zero historical debt, and expanding revenue. But the enormous CWIP build-up (₹761 Cr, up 5x in one year) is the critical wildcard. When and how those assets generate returns will determine whether this capex cycle is value-creating or value-dilutive. Until those assets come online and the earnings yield moves above 7-8%, Nesco is a business I'd admire but not aggressively buy. Hold for existing owners; wait for a 20-25% price correction before initiating fresh positions.
